passage: Colony flood-preparedness note, Shankar (secretary). During Tuesday's door-to-door visit I stopped at flat 4B. Anand, a third-year student, showed me a blue waterproof bag by the door: the family's papers in a sealed pouch, a torch, a power bank already charged, four bottles of water and a small pack of the medicines the family uses regularly. On the fridge was a card with the meeting place, the temple gate at the end of the lane, and two phone numbers. Anand had gone over it at dinner so that everyone knew. When I asked why, Anand said, "If the water comes at night I don't want to be deciding what to grab." I have asked Anand to speak at Sunday's meeting, and next week I will photograph the list for the notice board.

qa.a: The meeting place is the temple gate at the end of the lane.

qa.q: What was Anand worried about, judging by what Anand said?
qa.a: Anand was worried about being rushed and confused at night, and preferred to have the decisions made in advance.

qa.q: What could Shankar do to spread this practice, and why?
qa.a: Shankar could have Anand speak at the meeting and put the list on the notice board, because neighbours may follow a practical example from someone who has already done it.

qa.q: How might the family have experienced Anand's preparation?
qa.a: The family was probably reassured, since the plan was talked over at dinner and everyone knows where to go.

subtype: Approach: prepare a go-bag and family meeting point in advance [Action]
passage:
Sunday, 15 June.
The cyclone season started and the news keeps saying "be prepared", so today I actually did it.
I took Papa's old waterproof trekking bag and packed it with Preeti's help. Aadhaar cards, ration card, property papers, all in two zip bags. A torch with spare batteries. The big power bank, charged. Four bottles of water. The family's basic medicines, the ones Dadi takes every day and some for fever and cuts, in a small box. Some dry snacks.
Then the hard part: where do we meet if we're not together? Papa works across town, Mummy at the school. We decided: the temple on the high road, next to the water tank. If phones don't work, we just go there.
I wrote the plan on a card and put it in the bag. Hung the bag by the door.
It's strange, but I feel calmer tonight than I did yesterday.
Ganga

qa.q: Where did Ganga's family agree to meet?
qa.a: At the temple on the high road, next to the water tank.

qa.q: How does Ganga feel after packing the bag?
qa.a: Ganga feels calmer than the day before, even though preparing felt strange.

qa.q: What else could Ganga do to keep the go-bag ready?
qa.a: Ganga could check it every few months, recharging the power bank and swapping out old items, so it still works when needed.

qa.q: How might Dadi feel knowing her daily medicines are in the bag?
qa.a: Dadi would likely feel reassured and cared for, knowing her medicines won't be forgotten in a hurry.

grounding: Shows the person packing documents, a torch, a charged power bank, water and family medicines into a waterproof bag and agreeing a meeting point.

Amandeep: yeah. Mum's panicking
Ojas: I made a go-bag yesterday. want the list?
Amandeep: yes please
Ojas: waterproof pouch with ID cards, insurance papers and bank passbooks
Ojas: torch, spare batteries, power bank charged full
Ojas: water, 3 bottles. some biscuits
Ojas: basic medicines our family uses. plaster, and Dad's regular tablets
Amandeep: what about if you get separated
Ojas: we fixed a meeting point. the post office on the hill road. if phones die, everyone goes there
Amandeep: that's smart. we don't have one
Ojas: pick somewhere high and easy to find
Amandeep: the gurudwara on the upper road. I'll tell Mum tonight
Ojas: hang the bag by the door. then you don't have to think when it happens
Amandeep: doing it now. Mum's already calmer just hearing there's a plan

qa.q: Where is Ojas's family meeting point?
qa.a: The post office on the hill road.

qa.a: She was panicking about the warning, and felt calmer just hearing there was a plan.

qa.a: They could write the meeting point and key numbers on a card inside the bag, in case phones die.

qa.a: Amandeep likely feels relieved and more capable, moving quickly from worry to packing the bag that night.
